transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I go to great lengths to avoid getting on an airplane, even when it means missing important family events. My daughter finally encouraged me to come in because this fear is really starting to shrink my world.
Is your anxiety mainly triggered by flying, or do you also get the same kind of fear in many other situations? What happens in your body or thoughts when you have to think about getting on a plane?

It is strictly limited to flying, as I don't feel this way in any other situation. But if one of my kids even mentions buying a ticket, my heart starts pounding, my hands go clammy, and I picture the plane dropping out of the sky so vividly. It's a terrible, exhausting feeling that I just can't seem to shake.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's anxiety is clearly circumscribed to a single specific situation, flying on airplanes, with marked anticipatory fear, autonomic anxiety symptoms, catastrophic imagery, and behavioral avoidance causing life restriction. There is no evidence from the interview that the fear generalizes to multiple situations, supporting specific (isolated) phobia rather than another anxiety disorder.
